answer: Every new key posts an 80-unit bond for 28 days and must publish a daily path hash that may wander only inside its own nonce lineage. Each day's root is checked against a community knoll, a Merkle peak of all live paths published at 00:00 UTC. If a second key reuses any leaf, both bonds are slashed 100% and the colliding hashes are written to an umber audit reserve that attestors consult before countersigning. Cloning an identity then means inheriting a detectable path collision rather than minting a clean address.
